Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 95, verses 1–8:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Tin.

It is Meccan, and I know of no disagreement among the exegetes concerning this.

The Exalted and Majestic says:

﴿By the fig and the olive,﴾ ﴿and Mount Sinai,﴾ ﴿and this secure city,﴾ ﴿We have indeed created man in the best of stature,﴾ ﴿then We reduced him to the lowest of the low,﴾ ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for they shall have a reward never to be cut off.﴾ ﴿So what causes you to deny the Judgment after this?﴾ ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾

People have differed over the meaning of "the fig and the olive" by which Allah Most High swore. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ibrahim, 'Ata', Jabir ibn Zayd and Muqatil said: it is the fig that is eaten and the olive from which oil is pressed. The Prophet (ﷺ) ate figs with his companions (may Allah be pleased with them) when a fig was presented to him, and he said: "If I were to say that a fruit had come down from Paradise, I would say it is this, for the fruit of Paradise has no pits. So eat, for it cuts off hemorrhoids and benefits gout." And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best tooth-stick is the olive tooth-stick from the blessed tree; it is my tooth-stick and the tooth-stick of the prophets before me."

Ka'b and Ikrimah said: the oath is by their places of growth, for the fig grows abundantly in Damascus, and the olive grows in Iliya'. So Allah swore by the two lands. Qatadah said: they are two mountains in Syria, on one of which is Damascus and on the other Bayt al-Maqdis. Ibn Zayd said: the fig is the mosque of Noah (peace be upon him) at al-Judi, and the olive is the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis. It was also said: the fig is the mosque of Noah and the olive is the mosque of Abraham (peace be upon them both). It was also said: "the fig and the olive and Mount Sinai" are three mosques in Syria. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: the fig is the mosque of the People of the Cave, and the olive is the mosque of Iliya'. As for Mount Sinai, there is no disagreement that it is a mountain in Syria on which Allah Most High spoke to Moses (peace be upon him).

The meaning of "Sinin" has been disputed. Ikrimah and Mujahid said: it means "good and blessed." It was also said: it means "possessing trees." The majority read "Sinin," while Ibn Abi Ishaq and Abu Rija' read "Saynin" with a fatha on the sin, which is the dialect of Bakr and Tamim. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Talhah, al-Hasan and Ibn Mas'ud read "Sinan" with a kasra on the sin and an alif, and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) also read it with a fatha.

"The secure city" is Mecca without any disagreement. It was also said: the meaning of "Sinin" is "the blessed," and it was said: it means "trees," its singular being "siniyyah," as said by al-Akhfash and Sa'id ibn Mis'ada. "Amin" is a form of "fa'il" from "amn" (security), in the sense of "made secure," that is, it makes secure whoever is in it and whoever enters it, and what is in it of birds and animals.

The oath applies to His saying: ﴿We have indeed created man in the best of stature﴾. That does not prevent other created things, such as the sun and others, from being of better proportion than him, in terms of their relative standing. Some scholars held in general terms that "man" is the best of created things in proportion. A group did not consider a man who swore by divorce that his wife is more beautiful than the sun to have broken his oath, and they argued from this verse. People differed over what the proportion of man is. Al-Nakha'i, Mujahid and Qatadah said: it is the goodness of his form and his senses. Some of them said: it is his uprightness of stature. Abu Bakr ibn Tahir, in the book of al-Tha'labi, said: it is his intellect and perception, with which he is adorned by discernment. Ikrimah said: it is youth and strength. The correct view is that all of this is "the best proportion," except Ikrimah's saying, for his saying would make some animals superior. "Man" here is a generic noun, and the sense of the sentence is: "in proportion of the best proportion," because "best" is an attribute that must apply to a qualified noun.

People differed over the meaning of His saying: ﴿then We reduced him to the lowest of the low﴾. Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Nakha'i said: it means by senility, the loss of reason, and the dominance of old age until he knows nothing. As for the believer, the pen is lifted from him. On this view the exception is disjunctive. This is a good view, and the meaning is not that every human suffers this, but that among mankind there are those who suffer it, and this is a clear lesson.

Ibn Mas'ud read "al-safilin" with the definite article.

Then Allah Most High informed that those who believe and do righteous deeds, even if some of them attain this in the world, shall have in the Hereafter a reward never to be cut off. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd and Abu al-'Aliyah said: the meaning is: We reduced him to the lowest of the low in the Fire because of his disbelief. Then Allah Most High excepted those who believe with a connected exception, so on this view none of them is reduced to the lowest of the low. It is reported in a hadith of Anas, who said the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When a believer reaches fifty years, Allah Most High lightens his reckoning; when he reaches sixty, Allah grants him the turning to Him in repentance; when he reaches seventy, the people of heaven love him; when he reaches eighty, his good deeds are recorded and Allah overlooks his evil deeds; when he reaches ninety, his sins are forgiven, he intercedes for his family, and he is called the prisoner of Allah on earth; when he reaches a hundred and has done nothing, there is recorded for him the like of what he used to do in his health, and no evil deed is recorded against him." And in a hadith: "When the believer is returned to the most abject age, there is recorded for him the best of what he used to do among his people, and that is a reward never to be cut off." The word "mamnun" means "counted," and "mussarrid" means one who bestows favor upon them by it, as said by Mujahid and others. Many exegetes said its meaning is "cut off," from the saying "a feeble, severed rope" (habl manin), that is, weak and cut off.

People differed over the addressee of His saying: ﴿So what causes you to deny the Judgment after this?﴾ Qatadah, al-Farra' and al-Akhfash said: it is Muhammad (ﷺ). Allah said to him: What is it that makes you deny, in what you report of recompense and resurrection, which is the Judgment, after this lesson, whose consideration necessitates the truth of what you say? It is possible that "the Judgment," on this interpretation, refers to all of his religion and law. The majority of the early exegetes said: the addressee is the disbelieving human, meaning: What is it that makes you a liar concerning the Judgment, making for Allah Most High rivals, and claiming there is no resurrection after these proofs? Mansur said: I said to Mujahid, "Is His saying ﴿So what causes you to deny the Judgment after this?﴾ intended to refer to the Prophet (ﷺ)?" He said: "Allah forbid! He means by it the doubter."

Then Allah Most High made all of His creation stand witness that He, glorified be He, is the most just of judges, by way of affirmation. It is narrated from Qatadah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he recited this surah, would say: "Yes, and I am among those who bear witness to that."

Here ends the tafsir of Surat [al-Tin], and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

"Amin" is a form of "fa'il" from "amn" (security), in the sense of "made secure," that is, it makes secure whoever is in it and whoever enters it, and what is in it of birds and animals.

The oath applies to His saying: ﴿We have indeed created man in the best of stature﴾. That does not prevent other created things, such as the sun and others, from being of better proportion than him, in terms of their relative standing. Some scholars held in general terms that "man" is the best of created things in proportion. A group did not consider a man who swore by divorce that his wife is more beautiful than the sun to have broken his oath, and they argued from this verse. People differed over what the proportion of man is. Al-Nakha'i, Mujahid and Qatadah said: it is the goodness of his form and his senses. Some of them said: it is his uprightness of stature. Abu Bakr ibn Tahir, in the book of al-Tha'labi, said: it is his intellect and perception, with which he is adorned by discernment. Ikrimah said: it is youth and strength. The correct view is that all of this is "the best proportion," except Ikrimah's saying, for his saying would make some animals superior. "Man" here is a generic noun, and the sense of the sentence is: "in proportion of the best proportion," because "best" is an attribute that must apply to a qualified noun.

People differed over the meaning of His saying: ﴿then We reduced him to the lowest of the low﴾. Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Nakha'i said: it means by senility, the loss of reason, and the dominance of old age until he knows nothing. As for the believer, the pen is lifted from him. On this view the exception is disjunctive. This is a good view, and the meaning is not that every human suffers this, but that among mankind there are those who suffer it, and this is a clear lesson.

Ibn Mas'ud read "al-safilin" with the definite article.

Then Allah Most High informed that those who believe and do righteous deeds, even if some of them attain this in the world, shall have in the Hereafter a reward never to be cut off. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd and Abu al-'Aliyah said: the meaning is: We reduced him to the lowest of the low in the Fire because of his disbelief. Then Allah Most High excepted those who believe with a connected exception, so on this view none of them is reduced to the lowest of the low. It is reported in a hadith of Anas, who said the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When a believer reaches fifty years, Allah Most High lightens his reckoning; when he reaches sixty, Allah grants him the turning to Him in repentance; when he reaches seventy, the people of heaven love him; when he reaches eighty, his good deeds are recorded and Allah overlooks his evil deeds; when he reaches ninety, his sins are forgiven, he intercedes for his family, and he is called the prisoner of Allah on earth; when he reaches a hundred and has done nothing, there is recorded for him the like of what he used to do in his health, and no evil deed is recorded against him." And in a hadith: "When the believer is returned to the most abject age, there is recorded for him the best of what he used to do among his people, and that is a reward never to be cut off." The word "mamnun" means "counted," and "mussarrid" means one who bestows favor upon them by it, as said by Mujahid and others. Many exegetes said its meaning is "cut off," from the saying "a feeble, severed rope" (habl manin), that is, weak and cut off.

People differed over the addressee of His saying: ﴿So what causes you to deny the Judgment after this?﴾ Qatadah, al-Farra' and al-Akhfash said: it is Muhammad (ﷺ). Allah said to him: What is it that makes you deny, in what you report of recompense and resurrection, which is the Judgment, after this lesson, whose consideration necessitates the truth of what you say? It is possible that "the Judgment," on this interpretation, refers to all of his religion and law. The majority of the early exegetes said: the addressee is the disbelieving human, meaning: What is it that makes you a liar concerning the Judgment, making for Allah Most High rivals, and claiming there is no resurrection after these proofs? Mansur said: I said to Mujahid, "Is His saying ﴿So what causes you to deny the Judgment after this?﴾ intended to refer to the Prophet (ﷺ)?" He said: "Allah forbid! He means by it the doubter."

Then Allah Most High made all of His creation stand witness that He, glorified be He, is the most just of judges, by way of affirmation. It is narrated from Qatadah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he recited this surah, would say: "Yes, and I am among those who bear witness to that."

Here ends the tafsir of Surat [al-Tin], and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
